claims.text: The disordered HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy.
Random chemical occupation and atomic-size mismatch cause severe local lattice distortion in disordered HfNbTaTiZr.
Controlled annealing or Monte Carlo evolution can induce chemical short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr nucleates HfTi and TiZr B2-like ordered clusters.
Between approximately 800 K and 1200 K, the ordered clusters can form a percolating network without melting or phase decomposition.
A coherent network of B2-like clusters regularizes the local lattice potential and reduces the variance of atomic displacement amplitudes.
Formation of HfTi and TiZr ordered clusters relieves local atomic-size mismatch strain and reduces the global root-mean-square lattice distortion.
Reduced lattice distortion lowers the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
Percolating ordered clusters create continuous low-scattering pathways for phonon transport.
Ordering produces stiffer local bonds and shifts the high-frequency phonon density of states to higher frequencies.
The DOS shift and reduced distortion increase phonon group velocities.
Ordering increases phonon mean free paths and lifetimes.
The percolated SRO state has higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random solid-solution state.
High-frequency phonon modes have a smaller full-width at half-maximum in the ordered state.
Atoms within the ordered clusters have lower mean-square atomic displacements than in the random state.
Severe random-state lattice distortion is the dominant phonon-scattering mechanism in HfNbTaTiZr.
Below the ordered-cluster percolation threshold, isolated clusters act as scattering centers and decrease thermal conductivity.
Growth of the ordered phase into domains with incoherent interfaces terminates the conductivity-increase regime.
High-temperature entropy-driven disordering restores random lattice distortion and terminates the conductivity-increase regime.
Dominant interfacial scattering or elastic misfit from the ordered clusters would instead decrease thermal conductivity.
